steps.title: Rich and perfumed
steps.body: Viognier gives full-bodied whites with apricot, peach, honeysuckle, violet and orange blossom. Acidity is low to medium, alcohol often high, 13.5 to 14.5%, and the texture oily and round. It's aromatic yet dry, a combination that can surprise first-time tasters.

steps.title: Nearly lost
steps.body: Viognier is difficult to grow: low and irregular yields, prone to coulure, poor fruit set, and powdery mildew. By the mid-1960s, only about 14 hectares remained, mostly in Condrieu. Interest grew from the 1980s, and plantings spread to the south of France, California, Australia and beyond. Today there are over 15,000 hectares worldwide.

options: Low, irregular yields made it unprofitable
steps.explanation: Poor fruit set and disease gave low yields, so growers abandoned it.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: Look for medium to deep lemon or gold colour, an intense apricot and floral nose, and a full, round, oily palate with low acidity and warmth from alcohol. Compared with Gewürztraminer, it's more apricot than lychee, and less spicy.

steps.prompt: Viognier typically has very high acidity.
steps.explanation: Not true. Its acidity is low to medium, which gives it a round, oily texture.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Viognier gives apricot, honeysuckle and violet
It nearly vanished, with about 14 hectares in the 1960s
It's full, round and low in acidity
